title: India Gears Up for the 100th Edition of Fit India Sundays on Cycle on November 29
subtitle:
Union Sports Minister Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya to lead the landmark celebrations from Pune; to be joined by 50,000 cycling enthusiasts
#IndiaReady4Olympics: Celebrating the Olympic Movement and Strengthening India's Sporting Culture
Youth Across Every District to Join the 100th Sundays on Cycle Celebrations in Association with MY Bharat
100 Indian Olympians to Join Celebrations at 100 Iconic Locations Nationwide in Association with MY Bharat
body_text: Launched in December 2024, following the call of the Prime Minister Narendra Modi to make India a fitter and healthier nation, the Fit India Sundays on Cycle, has grown into a nationwide movement, bringing together people from all walks of life to promote fitness through cycling. The initiative began with just 250 locations and 500 participants in New Delhi. Over two years, Sundays on Cycle has grown into a people's movement. Its 99th edition, held on the theme of Constitution Day, saw lakhs of citizens participate at more than 26,000 locations across the country. Marking a significant milestone in this journey, the movement is now gearing up for the celebration of its 100th edition of Sundays on Cycle. The landmark edition of Sundays on Cycle is dedicated to celebrating the Olympic Movement in India, under the theme #IndiaReady4Olympics . Union Minister of Youth Affairs and Sports Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya will lead the 100th Sundays on Cycle celebrations from Pimpri-Chinchwad, Pune, where around 50,000 cyclists will join the movement. In association with MY Bharat, the 100th Sundays on Cycle will be celebrated by young people in every district across the country. Additionally, the celebrations will be organised across 100 prominent iconic locations nationwide, where 100 Indian Olympians will join in on the milestone celebration to pedal towards making India a fitter nation. The upcoming edition will celebrate the values at the heart of the Olympic Movement: good governance and integrity, fair competition and inclusion, the health and welfare of athletes, and a lasting legacy of sustainability and safe sport. It reflects India's commitment to building its sporting future on ethics, athlete voice and equal opportunity for all, including women and para-athletes, and seeks to inspire the youth to embrace sport and fitness as a way of life. The movement takes inspiration from Prime Minister's call of "Fitness ka Dose, Aadha Ghanta Roz" , with the aim of dedicating at least half an hour to fitness every day. The initiative has evolved into a platform for taking forward Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s key national calls and social messages, translating them into action through mass public participation. Through special editions centred on themes such as Fight Against Obesity, Nasha Mukt Bharat, Pollution Ka Solution, Sundays on Cycle seeks to encourage behavioural change and inspire citizens to contribute to the Prime Minister’s vision of a Fit India and a Viksit Bharat. ***** Ayushman Kumar
